title: Binary joint surface: does the binary-vs-float gap narrow when atoms, bits and data rise jointly (does the joint budget buy back M114's bit loss)?

device._note: sign-code projection on CPU numpy (float64); the Hamming GEMM (sign-GEMM identity, bit-identical to the CPU hardware-POPCNT path) on the GPU; ridge on CPU. HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1, gfx1201.

parity_guard.feature: CLS token concatenated with the mean of the patch tokens

sparse.dictionary_rule: at each atom count, the prefix of the seeded permutation of the shared 8192-whitened-patch pool (seed 11) - M108/M113/M114/M117/M118 exact, so (3072,108) is the sealed anchor
sparse.bits_construction: 108 bits = the single M114/M118 projection (ITQ seed 33 / seeded Gaussian seed 33). 216 bits = TWO INDEPENDENT 108-bit projections CONCATENATED (seeds 33 and 34 for ITQ, and 33 and 34 for the Gaussian control). Registered note: v19 section 5.1's heading says '256' but its construction sentence says 'two independent 108-bit projections concatenated' = 216; the construction is followed exactly (216 = 2 x 108). Disclosed: NOT a linear-cap violation - two independent projections of the SAME whitened patch, so the code is genuinely 216 bits and the encode cost is ~2x a 108-bit encode.
sparse.hamming: sign-GEMM identity (bit-identical to packed uint64 XOR + POPCNT); triangle kernel on Hamming, soft assignment over ALL atoms

scaling.subsample_rule: first n rows of the M107-shuffled train order (nested, deterministic)
scaling.test_set: the full 34500-row shared test set, identical for every cell and arm

reuse._note: the (atoms=3072, bits=108) cells are REUSED from M118's sealed code memmaps (data_cache_root/v16/m118/{arm}_{split}.npy) - the codes are image functions and M118's construction is identical (same whitener, same dictionary prefix, same hash seeds). The t1 gate below verifies the reuse mechanically by re-fitting b_random and c_itq at n=138000 against M118's sealed 0.1842 / 0.1820. All other cells are freshly encoded.

gate.t1_reference: reused (3072,108) cells re-fit at n=138000 must reproduce M118 sealed b_random 0.1842 and c_itq 0.1820 within 0.002, else the run voids
gate.kill_switch_1_joint_buyback: fired (fail) if for EITHER arm the binary-vs-float gap at (6144, 138000, 216 bits) does NOT narrow by >= 0.01 vs the gap at (3072, 138000, 108 bits). gaps use the M117 float references (0.2153 at 3072/138000, 0.2249 at 6144/138000). If the joint budget (wider head + more bits + more data) narrows the gap >= 0.01, the binary axis re-opens as a QUALITY route; if not, it is cost-only and M114/M118 verdicts stand.
gate.registered_prediction: M117 showed atoms help at full data; M118 showed the 108-bit loss is intrinsic at fixed atoms. If the loss is a fixed-capacity artifact, more bits (216) AND a wider head (6144) AND more data should narrow it; if the loss is intrinsic to the Hamming code itself, the gap persists.
